newsitem.title: USA: Yellow eliminates 102 jobs, sees more cuts.
newsitem.headline: Yellow eliminates 102 jobs, sees more cuts.

text.p: Yellow Freight System, the flagship subsidiary of Yellow Corp., Friday announced 102 job cuts and said another 65 to 70 jobs will be eliminated through normal attrition during the first half of the year.
In addition, 131 employees have chosen to accept early retirement packages offered to 153 workers who are 55 or older and had at least 20 years of service, the company said.
Yellow Freight, which provides freight services for commodities in North America, Europe and Asia/Pacific, has 24,000 employees.
The actions complete Yellow Freight's restructuring announced in December to sharpen customer focus and improve profitability.

The Overland Park, Kan.-based company said it will take an unspecified one-time charge in the fourth quarter for employee severance and retirement packages, write down certain assets and cover other restructuring costs.
Fourth-quarter and full-year 1996 financial results will be announced in about two weeks, it said.
Yellow Freight also said it has decentralized its operations into five business units that serve the Northeast, North-Central, Southeast, Central and Western regions.
Yellow Corp.'s stock fell 12.5 cents to $16.375 on Nasdaq in late trading.
